I am in Quzhou County, Hebei, at the start of the growing season, so I will stick with the cropping pattern I trust most for my land, labor, and age: winter wheat followed by summer maize. That is the most familiar and practical choice for me on the North China Plain. I am 65, so I will not choose crops that need too much hand labor or complicated field management. I will keep the system simple, stable, and mechanized as much as possible. I will use improved or hybrid seed because I want steady emergence, better stress tolerance, and more reliable yield than old saved seed. For wheat, I will manage fertilizer moderately, because too much nitrogen can cause lodging and waste money. I will still give enough phosphorus and potassium to support roots and grain filling. I will irrigate several times because rainfall is not always reliable here, especially in key stages. For maize, I will also use hybrid seed, because that is what gives me the most dependable production in my conditions. I will fertilize enough to support ear development, but I will not overdo it. I will use rotary tillage because it is easier and faster for me than deep ploughing every season, and it fits the wheat-maize rotation well. I will spray pesticides only as needed for common weeds, aphids, rusts, and maize pests, because I want to protect yield but keep costs controlled. My goal is not to chase the highest possible output. I will aim for a stable harvest, manageable work, and low risk.
